correctness.rationale: A private-neighbor injection using the vertical perfect matching bounds every minimal dominating set by n. For equality, full columns and empty columns are equinumerous; all 2k vertices in full columns need distinct outside private neighbors, which exhaust the 2k vertices in empty columns. This forbids adjacency to singleton columns and forces one unlike edge per column in the full/empty case, hence the unique path perfect matching and exactly two even-n words. In the singleton case private-neighbor viability forces period-two row choices, yielding exactly four words. Each word is directly shown minimal dominating. Independent exhaustive brute-force comparison for n=2..10 and all-subset total checks through n=9 passed; these support but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: A motivated complete classification of maximum inclusion-minimal dominating sets of every open ladder: the bipartite equality Γ=α explains only the size and checkerboard witnesses, whereas the theorem identifies all non-independent maximizers and a sharp odd/even change in their count. It provides the exact extremal coefficient of the minimal-domination size enumerator, useful for upper-domination benchmark instances and understanding equality in the matching bound, without artificial parameter choices.
